# Play implementation plan — Java 26.3 / protocol 777

Planning baseline: **2026-10-04**. Checked items and execution notes record implementation evidence; acceptance gates remain separate. M6 source includes private persistent overrides, bounded gateway-scoped chunk/action/mode views, pose-driven interest updates, backend-owned mode policy, reach/state/sequence/rate checks, atomic supported Survival inventory deltas, and callback-plus-subscription confirmation before block ACK. M7 source includes an admin-only profile mode grant, bounded client Survival/Adventure requests, all-mode ability/game-event synchronization, SpacetimeDB-persisted health/food/death guarded by a single active-session owner, bounded vertical gravity/platform landing, border clamping, Survival sprint food drain and same-dimension void death/respawn. Current local gates: 31 library tests, 108 binary tests (3 opt-in live tests ignored), 10 backend policy tests, root Clippy/format, optimized backend WASM compilation, SpacetimeDB packaging, and public binding freshness pass; SpacetimeDB packaging skips optional `wasm-opt` optimization because the executable is unavailable. The expanded disposable DB rollback/concurrency/vitals-reconnect harness compiles but remains unrun; graphical acceptance remains open. Computer Use approval rejected access to the running `javaw` process, so no screenshot evidence was recorded.

## Acceptance evidence reviewer — 2026-10-04

Added a standalone Rust evidence-bundle builder at `tools/jev/src/bin/evidence-review.rs`. It explicitly selects this plan, the roadmap, connection/gateway/Play codecs, backend foundation/world, and opt-in live-test source; records stable noncryptographic source fingerprints; audits direction-scoped packet counts; and prepares eight independent Choice questions with supported/contradicted/insufficient-evidence outcomes. It never treats a test definition as a passing execution record or auto-checks acceptance boxes.

Reviewer/harness unit tests passed (6 total), evidence generation ran, and the request passed schema dry-run. A subsequent authorized live Jev review used the credential from `tools/jev/.env` without printing or copying it. The original full-source request received HTTP 400; a bounded line-numbered excerpt request succeeded with pinned `jev-1.13.0` (17,605 input tokens; 403 output tokens). Jev contradicted claims of full codec, live-backend and M7 graphical acceptance, and found persistence/atomicity evidence insufficient in its excerpts; baseline/commit judgments had low confidence. Independent source inspection confirms same-reducer inventory/block updates and callback-plus-matching-subscription gating for successful edits, but does not establish host rollback or graphical behavior. No gameplay test, database mutation or graphical validation was performed in this review, and no milestone or packet acceptance was promoted. Detailed findings and limitations: [acceptance-evidence-review.md](acceptance-evidence-review.md).

### Granular follow-up — 2026-10-04

Four narrower Jev requests evaluated 32 checks using pinned `jev-1.13.0`: 19 source-support judgments, 7 contradictions and 6 insufficient-evidence results. These are not a completion score. Backend edit safeguards and worker callback/subscription gating received stronger source support; chunk reload ordering, vitals persistence and actual live/graphical acceptance remain open. A low-confidence mode-sync contradiction was not adopted because direct inspection shows all-mode Game Event emission. Follow-up inspection found a partial death/Respawn source path; a later local test now covers loading reset, stale inventory/block work and corrective-teleport readiness, while disposable-backend and graphical acceptance remain open. Detailed check-by-check results: [acceptance-evidence-granular-review.md](acceptance-evidence-granular-review.md). No acceptance checkbox was promoted.

### Fresh progress/action review — 2026-10-04

[Progress report](progress-review-20261004T230800Z/report.md) and [machine-readable actions](progress-review-20261004T230800Z/actions.json) record six passing local commands and four valid Jev batches (27 judgments). Persisted vitals ownership/reconnect and controlled death/respawn now receive source support. The worker batch failed typed validation; no result was accepted. `src/connection.rs` changed during the scan, so worker/player source judgments and local test records are snapshot evidence, **not verification of the latest file**. No live or graphical gate was promoted. Prioritize disposable-host rollback/race/restart coverage, component semantics and bounded-queue validation, then authorized two-client acceptance; avoid expanding gameplay scope.

### Current local integration checkpoint — 2026-10-04

The granular-review fingerprint manifest was checked before reusing its findings: `src/connection.rs`, `src/gateway.rs`, `src/foundation_live_tests.rs`, and `spacetimedb/src/world.rs` have changed since that review; `spacetimedb/src/policy.rs` still matches. Current targeted checks pass: `cargo test --bin rusty_mines chunk_` (4), `cargo test --bin rusty_mines block_actions` (1), `cargo test --bin rusty_mines persistent_respawn` (1), `cargo test --bin rusty_mines game_mode_state` (1), `cargo test -p rusty-mines-inventory` (15), `cargo test --manifest-path spacetimedb/Cargo.toml` (10), `cargo test --lib` (31), `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, the backend `wasm32-unknown-unknown` check, optimized backend `cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, and `spacetime build --module-path spacetimedb`. SpacetimeDB reported successful packaging but continued without optional `wasm-opt` optimization because `wasm-opt` is unavailable. Public-only Rust binding generation succeeded and all 76 generated files exactly match `src/module_bindings`; private-table-inclusive output is intentionally not the application binding set. The full binary suite also passed 108 tests with 3 opt-in live tests ignored. This validates current local code only: the live database and graphical gates remain open, and Adventure editing remains fail-closed until authoritative `CanBreak`/`CanPlaceOn` permission semantics are implemented.

The inventory fixture test now cross-checks every one of the 122 official component IDs/names against the pinned protocol schema before decoding the matching component samples and their truncated prefixes. The fixture mapping check, all 15 inventory tests, all 31 root library tests, inventory Clippy, and backend WASM check pass after this change. This verifies schema/fixture alignment and bounded parsing; it does not establish gameplay semantics for arbitrary component effects or hashed non-default patches.

A fresh offline run of `tools/jev`'s local roadmap auditor reports 213 unique `(direction, ID)` rows and no duplicates: 25 I, 41 P, 147 deferred. The directional split is CB 21 I/12 P/111 deferred and SB 4 I/29 P/36 deferred; it matches the roadmap's current total. The auditor verifies row keys/status counts only, not field-level packet correctness or acceptance. Its two unit tests pass; no AI review or network request was made.

The current live world-action harness is disposable-database-only: it edits fixed coordinates including `(8,63,8)` and `(15,63,15)`, and `remove_session_state` deletes interest/action sequencing state but does not delete persistent `block_override` rows. Do not run it against the shared main database; doing so would leave test edits in the world. The reachable local server currently exposes only `quickstart-chat`, and no `SPACETIMEDB_TEST_*` credentials are present.

`README.md` now documents the exact ignored M6/M7 world-action test command and its persistent-row behavior, alongside the gateway lifecycle test setup. Listing the ignored test with that command succeeded; it was not executed against a database.

The ignored M6/M7 harness now additionally reconnects the same gateway identity, creates a new profile session, restores its pose/world interest, and asserts that the subscribed chunk snapshot contains the prior committed override. The exact ignored test compiles, formats, and passes Clippy, but remains unexecuted until a disposable database and test token are available; this is source-level coverage, not restart acceptance.

## Sources and current baseline

The [Play packet roadmap](play-packet-roadmap.md) remains the packet inventory/status source of truth. Its pinned [Minecraft Wiki revision](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets?oldid=3810839) and the official 26.3 codecs must be checked for field-level work; do not substitute older protocol layouts. This plan sequences deliverables rather than duplicating its 213 inventory rows.

Read project constraints in [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) and [.windsurfrules](../.windsurfrules) before implementation. Reducers are atomic and deterministic; sender/connection ownership is mandatory; subscription state supplies data, not reducer return values. Auto-increment IDs may have gaps and are never an ordering mechanism.

Reviewed implementation anchors:

| Source | Current behavior and consequence |
| --- | --- |
| [connection.rs](../src/connection.rs), `ClientSession`, `handle_configuration`, `handle_play`, `poll` | Login → Configuration → wire Play; backend Play after initial teleport acknowledgement plus Player Loaded or the 60-tick fallback. Server owns normal-mode Y/gravity/landing, bounded horizontal deltas and world-border correction; authorized Creative/Spectator flight accepts bounded Y. Sprint drains Survival food on server ticks; void fall resets to the same-dimension spawn. Pose writes remain bounded/asynchronous. |
| [play.rs](../src/packets/play.rs), `Serverbound::decode`, packet writers/patch helpers | Chat session arrays enforce 512-byte public-key and 4096-byte signature bounds; client ground/collision flags are advisory only; mode and flight requests are bounded. Abilities, Health and Game Event use protocol 777 IDs. Creative Slot is decoded into the bounded shared Slot model and submitted to backend policy. |
| [vanilla_world.rs](../src/vanilla_world.rs) | Official 26.3 flat-platform chunks stream in a movement-centered window; client view distance is capped at radius 2. Block overrides persist and gateway-scoped snapshots are applied to loaded chunks. Physics is intentionally limited to the platform and world border; death recovery reuses the initial-dimension spawn. |
| [foundation.rs](../spacetimedb/src/foundation.rs) | Private gateway/profile/session/entity/pose tables, gateway-scoped public views. Indexed ownership requires gateway identity **and** connection. Matching begin/phase retries are idempotent; expired leases cannot be renewed by retry or phase transition. Bounded heartbeats renew `last_activity`; scheduled cleanup, disconnect and revoke remove sessions/entity/pose state. `update_player_states` validates bounded batches atomically and `gateway_world_players` exposes Play pose only to registered gateway identities. |
| [policy.rs](../spacetimedb/src/policy.rs) | Pure native-testable offline identity, ownership, administrator and phase policies. `Verified` exists but is not proof that online authentication is implemented. |
| [gateway.rs](../src/gateway.rs) | SDK subscriptions to gateway lifecycle/profile/pose views; transition confirmation combines reducer outcome and matching subscribed rows. M4 batches/coalesces bounded pose writes asynchronously and routes view changes through bounded per-client queues. Cleanup handles late begin commits. Saved-token behavior fails closed and must remain unchanged. |
| [foundation.rs](../spacetimedb/src/foundation.rs), [connection.rs](../src/connection.rs) | Backend `session_entity` allocates unique u64 IDs with checked positive i32 conversion. The gateway returns the confirmed owned Configuration row's ID and the worker uses it for wire Play Login; no process-local allocator remains. |
| [ExtractWorldInitialization.java](../tools/ExtractWorldInitialization.java), [RunWorldExtractor.java](../tools/RunWorldExtractor.java) | Official packet encode/decode and section checks underpin fixtures. They prove those samples, not arbitrary runtime chunk/Slot codecs. |
| [inventory-core](../inventory-core/src/lib.rs), [inventory.rs](../spacetimedb/src/inventory.rs), [inventory_registry.rs](../src/inventory_registry.rs) | Versioned registry metadata and schema-driven Slot/Hashed Slot codecs feed a deliberately small item policy, private per-player inventory, revisions, bounded retries, Creative permission, click/cursor rules, simple shared storage, and a few recipes. Codec coverage does not imply gameplay support for arbitrary items/components. |
| [players.rs](../src/players.rs), [vanilla_world.rs](../src/vanilla_world.rs), [foundation.rs](../spacetimedb/src/foundation.rs), [world.rs](../spacetimedb/src/world.rs) | M4 replication is scoped to the registered gateway identity's sender-scoped view. M6 reducer writes private overrides and atomic Survival inventory deltas; sender-scoped chunk/action/mode views feed loaded chunks and commit-confirmed ACKs. Supported edits are stone/grass surface operations under Survival/Creative rules; Adventure remains denied without supported permission components. Cross-gateway terrain sharing and live persistence acceptance remain open. |
| [foundation.rs](../spacetimedb/src/foundation.rs), [gateway.rs](../src/gateway.rs), [connection.rs](../src/connection.rs), [players.rs](../src/players.rs) | M5 now preserves and routes bounded unsigned player chat through sender-owned backend reducers and gateway-scoped subscriptions, enforces hidden/commands-only policy, and delivers it as unsigned System Chat. `/help`, `/inventory`, and `/storage` are handled; signed chat remains unverified and refused. |
| [foundation_live_tests.rs](../src/foundation_live_tests.rs) | Opt-in disposable-database tests; do not publish/reset databases or access saved gateway credentials automatically. Inventory and world/mode reducer tests compile with generated bindings but require an explicitly provisioned administrator token to exercise transactions; broad race/rollback and graphical checks remain open. A local in-memory publish validated runtime schema/view registration, not reducer behavior. |

This is an executable implementation plan. The user's active goal authorizes code, tests, backend module/binding updates, and document changes needed to complete it. Database publication/reset and graphical-client acceptance remain separate gates recorded under the relevant milestones; never target production or reuse saved gateway credentials for disposable tests.

## Scope and decisions before widening behavior

**Current implementation vs selected target:** source exposes a flat bounded world, restricted M3 inventory, narrow M6 edits, all four mode identifiers, and a limited M7 simulation. Every logged-in offline player may edit only under implemented mode policy; Adventure changes remain denied because the supported inventory policy does not yet evaluate `CanDestroy`/`CanPlaceOn`. Offline usernames/UUIDs remain labels, not authenticated identities.

Record answers at these checkpoints:

1. **M1:** pinned official 26.3 bytecode confirms that `ServerPlayer.tick()` decrements `clientLoadedTimeoutTimer`, initialized/reset to 60 by `restartClientLoadTimerAfterRespawn()`. Player Loaded clears it; Client Tick End only resets movement bookkeeping. The gateway currently approximates the server tick loop using monotonic 50 ms intervals from wire Play entry, reset by `reset_loading`; neither client tick bursts nor ordinary packets advance it. Preserve independent teleport readiness. A later simulation loop must supply actual server ticks.
2. **M2 — decided:** fail closed when SpacetimeDB availability or lease confirmation is lost; disconnect affected sessions promptly. Keep the implemented 5-second heartbeat, 30-second lease, bounded batches and expiry sweeps. Never restore old connection ownership implicitly.
3. **M3:** user selected **full component schema coverage** on 2026-10-04. The source now has schema-driven codecs for all known component schema kinds; complete fixture and field-semantics validation remains open. Keep the separate narrow item/write policy. Vanilla does not offer an invented Slot codec-subset negotiation; game-mode/edit permissions remain separate decisions.
4. **M4:** same-world/same-authorized-gateway-identity multiplayer is implemented in source. Cross-gateway visibility remains a separate extension with world-interest-authorized reads, not a global session-table subscription.
5. **M6 — decided:** enable supported block edits for every logged-in player, subject to normal mode restrictions: Survival and Creative may edit according to server policy; Adventure follows vanilla permission/item rules; Spectator remains non-mutating. Do not make the admin inventory permission gate ordinary world edits. Keep world/chunk writes bounded and persistent. The user selected edits “enabled by default,” “all players, all modes,” and normal mode rules on 2026-10-04.
6. **M7 — decided:** implement Survival, Creative, Adventure and Spectator, including authorized mode changes, the planned player-state/respawn/physics loop, and mode-appropriate interactions. This means all four game modes, not every vanilla mechanic or full Survival parity. Online authentication and verified signed chat remain separate optional projects, not prerequisites for the offline demo.

These gates record decisions or validation still needed; they are not a claim that every listed item is unimplemented. Current M1–M7 source work and remaining validation are recorded below. The M3 codec schema is broad, while the supported gameplay item policy is intentionally narrow. The selected all-mode edit policy follows each game's mode rules; unsupported Adventure component rules fail closed.

## Sequence, dependencies and size

P0 = correctness/safety prerequisite for the next enabled behavior. P1 = later functionality after its preceding gate. Sizes are relative complexity/risk, **not days**; capacity and desired vanilla fidelity are unknown.

| Milestone | Roadmap batches | Depends on | Complexity | Demonstrable exit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| M1 Harden static Play | 1, immediate 4/5 dependencies | Current baseline | Medium | Load with explicit packet or exact 60-tick fallback; recover from boundary movement with acknowledged corrections. |
| M2 Lease/retry-safe backend | Foundation support | Existing foundation; integrate after M1 | Medium–high | Retried lifecycle calls are safe; stale ownership expires; operator sees bounded lifecycle diagnostics. |
| M3a/b/c Inventory | 2 | M1 + M2 for authority/writes | High | Current source has snapshots, restricted Creative/click operations, one simple storage menu and a tiny recipe set; remaining codec review, live authorization/isolation and graphical gates must pass before calling the milestone validated. |
| M4a/b Multiplayer | 3 | M1 + M2; M3 codecs for equipment | High | Same-authorized-gateway-identity visibility and packet flow implemented; live two-client/graphical and backpressure gates remain. No combat claim. |
| M5 Offline chat/commands | 4 | M1 + M2; M4 visibility/routing | Medium | Source routing, rate/policy checks and small commands implemented; disposable backend and two-client graphical acceptance remain. |
| M6a/b Streaming and edits | 5 | M1 + M2 + M4 interest; M3b for item-dependent writes | Very high | Bounded streaming/unloads and persisted supported edits under each implemented mode rule; disposable-backend peer/reload acceptance remains open and Adventure edits fail closed pending component policy. |
| M7 All player game modes and survival loop | 6; deferred combat from 3 | M1 + M3 + M4 + M6 | Very high | Server-authoritative Survival, Creative, Adventure and Spectator transitions, state and supported mechanics with correction and persistence. |
| M8 Selected optional features | 7–8 and deferred controls | Relevant preceding gates | Feature-dependent | Individually accepted optional behavior; no claim of complete protocol coverage. |

M2's backend policy/schema work can proceed alongside M1 **only with disjoint ownership**: M1 owns `connection.rs`, `play.rs`, world fixtures/extractor; M2 owns backend `foundation.rs`/`policy.rs`. Serialize integration in `gateway.rs`, generated bindings, live tests and roadmap edits. Startup world assets remain static throughout M1–M5; do not make backend lease progress depend on terrain generation. Inventory fixture research and later chunk-codec research may run separately, but neither widens runtime acceptance before its gates.

## M1 — P0 static Play hardening first

**Goal:** correct loading, reusable teleports and bounded controls without enabling gameplay writes.

**Expected writes:** [connection.rs](../src/connection.rs), [play.rs](../src/packets/play.rs), [vanilla_world.rs](../src/vanilla_world.rs), official fixtures through [ExtractWorldInitialization.java](../tools/ExtractWorldInitialization.java), and owning rows in [roadmap](play-packet-roadmap.md). No new backend reducer/schema is required for the core hardening; retain `enter_play_session` semantics and the `SessionStore` fake-backend seam.

- [x] **P0** Separate wire Play, loading criterion, pending teleport, and backend-confirmed Play. Implement a saturating 60-server-tick fallback using the nominal clock described above. `PlayerLoaded` or fallback satisfies loading only; **60 ticks before teleport acknowledgement must never claim backend Play/loaded readiness**. Promote once only when loading criterion AND current initial teleport acknowledgement hold and backend confirmation succeeds. Virtual-clock tests cover idle fallback and client tick floods; graphical-client smoke remains pending.
- [x] **P0** Split Player Session bounds: public key ≤512 bytes, signature ≤4096; exact consumption, negative/oversized lengths rejected. This is structural validation, not certificate/signature verification. Cryptographic verification remains out of scope.
- [x] **P0** Preserve on-ground/horizontal-collision movement flags and validate all defined bits; retain them as inputs, not proof of physics. Apply finite validated Use Item rotation before supported item-use policy, even while the action remains read-only.
- [x] **P0** Introduce reusable pending teleport state: positive checked IDs, expected position/rotation, deadline and acknowledgement policy. The implementation permits one outstanding correction, rejects mismatched acknowledgements, handles ID exhaustion, and cleans up on disconnect. Initial loading readiness remains independent of later corrections.
- [x] **P0** Encode/patch arbitrary authoritative corrective position/rotation/velocity/flags according to official 777 layout. Initial static fixture validation remains separate. Finite out-of-static-box movement is corrected to the last accepted pose; malformed/nonfinite input still fails safely.
- [x] **P0** Route time-dependent state through an injectable/explicit monotonic clock seam. Absolute loading deadlines, keepalive timing, teleport deadlines, and cleanup are covered without sleep-based timing tests.
- [x] **P1** State explicit unsupported policies for reconfiguration, cookies, transfer and plugin channels. The README and packet roadmap now record those policies; codec tests keep Play cookie/reconfiguration/ping replies unsupported. Status Ping remains distinct from Play Ping. Add any Play ping/pong or reconfiguration support only as a separately tested request/state flow; do not accept acknowledgements for nonexistent requests.

**In scope:** static radius-2 world, existing Creative policy, structural bounds, readiness and correction lifecycle. **Out:** terrain, physics engine, authenticated chat, inventory mutation, entity replication, cookie/transfer support by default.

**Gate:** automated unit/virtual-clock tests cover 59/60/61 ticks, tick ordering, fallback-before-ack and ack-before-fallback, explicit loaded ordering, wrong/replayed teleport, correction deadlines/exhaustion, backend refusal and exactly-once promotion. Codec tests cover malformed bounds, nonfinite movement, flags, and VarInt teleport IDs; loopback covers fragmented/coalesced frames and cleanup. Manual 26.3 smoke—especially boundary correction and fallback loading—remains pending.

### M1 execution record — 2026-10-04

- Final `cargo test`: 20 library tests and 79 binary tests passed; one explicitly gated disposable-backend test ignored. Existing loopback tests passed. Roadmap totals remain I=6, P=38, unimplemented=169; this change improves existing partial handling without adding packet IDs.
- Corrected the client-packet-driven fallback using the pinned server bytecode. Virtual-clock coverage includes the instant before tick 60, idle completion, 100 client Tick End packets at frozen time, independent teleport readiness, reset, backend refusal and cleanup.
- Added `assets/teleport-26.3.json`: ten official corrective positions with signed coordinates, nonzero velocity/rotation, five positive VarInt ID boundaries and empty/all relative flags. Rust encoding must match every official sample byte-for-byte. The Java extractor decodes and re-encodes those exact bytes with full consumption.
- Existing static world extraction reproduced SHA-256 `3399bcbd9b4de58314c94a6de64c8675015b206b5e107e1e9f6be8aaa0169275`; all nine packets and 24 chunk sections passed official roundtrips.
- Graphical-client smoke remains pending. The automated connection/loopback suite is distinct from this manual gate. Disposable live backend checks remain pending and are not inferred from local tests.
- M2 review found wire Login used `AtomicI32`; the subsequent M2 execution below resolves that integration. M3 implementation has since been added; its validation gates remain open. M4–M8 remain future work.

## M2 — P0 backend leases, retries and observability

**Goal:** authoritative sessions remain bounded and ownership-safe under retry, crash, revoke and reconnect.

**Expected writes:** [foundation.rs](../spacetimedb/src/foundation.rs), [policy.rs](../spacetimedb/src/policy.rs), [gateway.rs](../src/gateway.rs), [gateway_dashboard.rs](../src/gateway_dashboard.rs), [players.rs](../src/players.rs), [foundation_live_tests.rs](../src/foundation_live_tests.rs); regenerate [module_bindings](../src/module_bindings/) after reviewed schema changes. Keep credential/session token storage semantics unchanged.

- [x] **P0** Make `begin_offline_session`, `advance_login_session`, `enter_play_session` retry-safe only for the same immutable request/session, gateway sender and owner connection. Already-achieved phase may succeed; conflicting payload, backwards transitions or a different connection must fail. Preserve duplicate active-player rejection and late-commit cleanup. Reducers now treat the same owned request/phase as idempotent; conflicting session UUID ownership/profile still fails. Backend live retry/rollback coverage remains pending.
- [x] **P0** Add bounded heartbeat reducer and lease fields, indexed expiry, deterministic scheduled cleanup using `ctx.timestamp`. Heartbeats validate every session's sender + connection, cannot revive expired/revoked sessions, and run independently of Minecraft packet traffic. Expiry and renewal race within transactions; cleanup rechecks current expiry before deletion. The gateway renews owned sessions every 5 seconds in bounded batches; disposable live renewal/expiry-race coverage remains pending.
- [x] **P0** Add composite `(gateway_identity, owner_connection)` ownership access where appropriate rather than scanning a gateway's sessions at disconnect. Check actual SpacetimeDB 2.10 index/view support; migrations must not assume new defaults apply to key/unique/auto-inc columns. The 2.10.2 module build accepts `by_gateway_connection`; the disconnect hook now queries this index.
- [x] **P0** Reuse backend `session_entity.id` → checked positive i32 `entity_id` for wire self Login. The gateway returns it only after reducer success and an owned Configuration subscription row; the worker rejects nonpositive IDs before world output. No narrowing casts, sequential assumptions, timestamp ordering from IDs, or process-local allocator. Lifetime i32 exhaustion fails allocation; host transaction rollback remains a live-test gate.
- [x] **P1** Add administrator-only lease/session views and bounded diagnostics: age, phase, lease remaining, last error and expiration counts. New views return no data to non-administrators, cap session rows at 128, and expose no token or inventory fields. Expiration totals are persisted; the local gateway dashboard continues to report its bounded last-failure reason. View time is sampled by the five-second cleanup reducer because SpacetimeDB 2.10 `ViewContext` has no clock. Local native tests and WASM compilation pass; disposable live-view authorization/rollback checks remain pending.

**Out:** transferring live sessions between connections/gateways, online player authentication, world generation.

**Gate:** pure policy tests plus disposable live tests for authorization, same-identity/different-connection denial, retries with conflicting payloads, duplicate-player races, renew/expire races, revocation, disconnect, rollback on entity i32 exhaustion and private-view isolation. Schema/WASM compile, binding regeneration and compatibility review are gates before any authorized test publication. Native policy tests alone do not prove host rollback or view security.

### M2 local execution record — 2026-10-04

- Applied ECC `rust-patterns`, `rust-testing` and `security-review` guidance without sub-agents. Codex's native ECC plugin refresh verified version 2.2.3 installed/enabled.
- Completed owned backend entity-ID delivery through `SessionStore::configure` to wire Login. Regression tests cover arbitrary positive IDs through i32 MAX, wrong session/gateway/connection/phase, invalid IDs, no world output on rejection and exactly-once cleanup.
- Added a shared expiry precondition to matching begin retries, Configuration/Play transitions and heartbeats. Native tests cover the instant before/at/after expiry, invalid durations and arithmetic overflow; expired sessions cannot be revived while awaiting scheduled cleanup.
- Fixed the heartbeat startup race and observed reducer outcomes. Session-batch rejection records diagnostics and uses the next current snapshot, so ordinary concurrent disconnects do not kick unrelated clients. Enqueue/internal failures disconnect the gateway; subscribed removal or loss of backend availability closes affected workers on their next poll, using the current wire disconnect format. Idle-worker tests cover Login, Configuration and confirmed Play.
- Authorized gateway enrollment also establishes a missing five-second cleanup schedule for additive upgrades that do not rerun init. Existing schedules are retained; host scheduling and upgrade behavior require live validation.
- Local checks: 20 library + 82 binary tests passed, one disposable-backend test ignored; eight native backend policy tests passed. Gateway and backend Clippy passed with warnings denied; release WASM compilation passed. All 28 regenerated Rust binding files match the checked-in bindings, so no schema migration or binding replacement is required for these changes.
- Updated the opt-in live harness for matching lifecycle retries, conflicting requests, connection ownership, heartbeat bounds/rollback and administrator-view isolation. It compiles but was **not run**; the user explicitly requested local checks with live validation pending. Renew/expiry races and host rollback on ID exhaustion remain pending, alongside the graphical M1 smoke gate. No database publication/reset occurred.

### M2 deployment compatibility repair — 2026-10-04

- Anonymous read-only schema inspection confirmed Maincloud `rusty-mines-5gxbr` has the earlier foundation/entity-ID schema but no heartbeat reducer or lease tables/views. Calling the new reducer against that deployment reached the internal-failure path and disconnected the gateway.
- Added a separate optional lease-view subscription. Heartbeats stay disabled until that subscription applies; unsupported lease capability records an explicit upgrade-required diagnostic while leaving required foundation subscriptions connected. Full M2 transport/internal heartbeat failures still fail closed after capability confirmation.
- The explicit anonymous read-only SDK probe passed against Maincloud: the lease query failed as expected, required subscriptions applied, and the connection remained active. It never loads saved credentials, calls reducers, publishes or resets a database. Its named test is ignored by default; this connectivity probe does not satisfy M2's disposable live lifecycle/rollback gates.
- Regression suite: 82 binary tests passed, two explicit live probes ignored by default; Clippy passed with warnings denied. The normal debug executable rebuilt successfully after the user stopped the running server and released the Windows file lock. Restart validation remains pending.

## M3 — authoritative inventory in three gated increments

**Goal:** maintain authoritative inventory state without treating client hashes as authority. The source has moved beyond the original planned state: bounded runtime Slot and Hashed Slot codecs, private inventory state, gateway snapshots, revision-checked requests, a restricted Creative policy, basic player clicks, simple storage, and a few recipes are present. This is a deliberately narrow gameplay policy. Full wire decoding does not permit arbitrary item/component effects, drops, arbitrary containers, or complete crafting parity.

**Existing implementation surfaces:** [inventory-core](../inventory-core/src/lib.rs), [inventory.rs](../spacetimedb/src/inventory.rs), [inventory_registry.rs](../src/inventory_registry.rs), [connection.rs](../src/connection.rs), [gateway.rs](../src/gateway.rs), [foundation.rs](../spacetimedb/src/foundation.rs), and generated bindings. Remaining work is primarily fixture/schema review, gate validation, any corrections that review exposes, and roadmap status reconciliation; do not create a second inventory codec or state model.

### M3a — P0 schema, codec and read-only snapshots

#### M3a extraction and verification record — 2026-10-04

Extend tests to prove edits and player vitals survive unload/reload, reconnect and gateway/backend restart without item duplication or cross-session writes. Then validate all modes, supported edits, movement/removal, queue pressure, inventory/storage/crafting, unsigned chat and controlled Survival death/respawn with two official 26.3 clients. Keep every milestone unaccepted until its live and graphical gates pass. Independently review all 122 component schemas/hash semantics and extend click/drag/revocation-race coverage; graphical inventory and M1 lifecycle smokes remain open.

The selected core demo after **M1–M7** targets two same-authorized-gateway offline clients loading/moving/seeing each other, supported inventory/storage/crafting, unsigned chat, bounded terrain, four modes, mode-permitted edits, controlled same-dimension death/respawn, and persistent world/player state. Current source includes M4 replication, M5 chat, bounded M6 streaming and edits, and limited M7 mode/state/physics/food/void death/respawn behavior. Completion remains open: local Rust tests, Clippy/format, backend WASM-target check, bindings generation and module release build pass; disposable-backend reducer mutation/reconnect/restart tests and all graphical acceptance remain unrun. Adventure edits fail closed until item permission components are supported. M1–M5 live/graphical acceptance remains. Cross-gateway entity/world visibility, generalized terrain, online auth, signed chat and optional packets are deferred.
